title: Strict inert affine covers with eigenparameter rigidifications
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian quasi-excellent regular separated scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $B$ be a $G$-strict strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and let a finite group $G$ act tamely on $(X,B)$, freely on $X\setminus B$, with abelian geometric inertia. There is a surjective $G$-equivariant etale map $h:U\to X$ with $U$ affine and a $G$-invariant strict normal crossings divisor $\overline B_U\supset h^{-1}B$ such that the action on $(U,\overline B_U)$ is very tame. Its divisorial log structure is fs log regular [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Here very tame means that geometric inertia has invertible order and acts trivially on the characteristic monoid and on the strict local log stratum. The map $(U,h^{-1}B)\to(X,B)$ is strict and inert: it pulls back the log structure and induces isomorphisms of geometric inertia groups. The affine cover may be obtained from finitely many neighborhoods for inertia subgroups by induction of their actions to $G$. Locally at a point with inertia $H$, after adjoining the roots of unity of order $|H|$, the components of $h^{-1}B$ and of $\overline B_U$ have equations among an $H$-eigenvector regular system of parameters. Pulling back this cover along a strict inert etale morphism again gives such local rigidifications.

source.place: VIII Lemmas 5.3.5 and 5.3.7, printed pp.124--125; very-tame locus openness in Lemma 5.3.2, p.123.
